title: The reproducible workstation
purpose: See the reproducible workstation as one install flow.
explanation: Your configuration lives in a versioned dotfiles repository. An install script links those files into place, producing a shell, git, and editor setup that any new machine can reproduce in minutes.
alt: Four steps left to right: a dotfiles repo feeds an install script, which creates shell, git and editor settings, which make any new machine ready to work.

learning_check.question: Which file makes the setup reproducible on a new machine?
learning_check.answer: The dotfiles repository, because it holds the configuration and the install script that links it into place.

title: Merge or rebase: two ways to integrate a branch
purpose: Tell apart the two ways Git integrates one branch into another, and predict what each does to the history.
explanation: Two branches diverge from a common ancestor C2: main adds C3, the feature branch adds C4. A merge combines the two tips with C2 in a three-way merge and records the result in a commit with two parents. A rebase replays C4's change on top of C3 as a new commit, so main can then fast-forward to it. Both end with the same files; only the history differs (Pro Git, Git Branching, sections Basic Branching and Merging and Rebasing).
alt: Flow from a shared commit C2: main gains C3, a feature branch gains C4, then a choice. Merge runs a three-way merge of C2, C3 and C4 and creates a commit with two parents. Rebase replays C4 on C3, creating a new commit that main fast-forwards to.

learning_check.question: Both paths end with the same file contents. What is actually different?
learning_check.answer: Only the history: merge keeps both lines and adds a commit with two parents, while rebase writes new commits in a straight line and abandons the originals.

purpose: Show how one command line hands its output to the next command through a pipe, so the learner can read and build a chain.
explanation: You type one command line. Each program writes text to standard output (STDOUT). The pipe symbol takes that text out of the screen and feeds it into the next program as standard input (STDIN). The last program writes its result to the terminal. The example is the article's own chain: curl fetches the response headers with -L to follow redirects and -I for headers only, grep keeps the lines that contain 'location', and awk prints the origin in front of the path in the second field.
alt: Flow diagram: you type one line, curl -L -I writes headers to STDOUT, a pipe feeds grep location, grep writes matching lines to STDOUT, a second pipe feeds awk, awk prints the origin plus the path, and the terminal shows one full URL.

learning_check.question: In `ls | wc -l`, which program reads from standard input, and what does the terminal show?
learning_check.answer: wc reads the text that ls wrote to STDOUT, counts its lines, and prints only that count to the terminal. You never see the file list.

title: How a pipe connects one command to the next
nvm's modules and how they call each other
purpose: See how one shell script is split into responsibilities that call each other.
explanation: The installer bootstraps nvm, the router dispatches each command, resolution turns a request into a version, and download plus install fetch and verify it. Each arrow matches a function call cited in the architecture note.
alt: A flowchart: the user reaches either install-script or the cli-dispatch router, the router calls version resolution and alias listing, and both lead into download-and-security and then install-node.

learning_check.question: Which module writes the new node onto the PATH?
learning_check.answer: versions-and-nvmrc, via nvm_change_path, after install-node has installed the binary.

title: One nvm install request end to end
purpose: Follow one `nvm install 22` through resolution, download, verification, and the PATH rewrite.
explanation: The command resolves the shorthand to a version, fetches the version index, downloads the tarball, verifies its checksum, then rewrites PATH. Each message is a function call cited in the architecture note.
alt: A sequence diagram where the user calls nvm install, the router resolves the alias, download-and-security returns a verified tarball, install-node installs it, and versions-and-nvmrc rewrites PATH.

learning_check.question: Which step must pass before the tarball is moved into the cache?
learning_check.answer: The checksum comparison, so an unverified archive is never cached.

title: The AI review loop
purpose: See how a sandbox and approvals keep an AI agent's edits safe to merge.
explanation: The sandbox sets technical boundaries and the approval policy decides when the agent must stop and ask.
alt: You prompt the agent with context. It proposes an edit inside a workspace-write sandbox. Tests run in the same boundary, then you read the diff and merge only when it passes.

learning_check.question: What does the sandbox boundary control, and what does the approval policy decide?
learning_check.answer: The sandbox controls which files the agent can edit and whether commands can use the network; the approval policy decides when the agent must stop and ask.

timeline.heading: Inside the sandbox vs beyond it

title: Dotfiles install: repo to $HOME via symlinks
purpose: See how one install script turns a dotfiles repo into a live home-directory setup.
explanation: install.sh loops over each config file, skips a link that already points at it, backs up any real file, then symlinks the repo file into $HOME.
alt: Config files gitconfig, zshrc and vimrc flow into install.sh, which checks for an existing link, backs up a real file, and creates a symlink into the home directory.

learning_check.question: Why does install.sh back up a real .zshrc before linking?
learning_check.answer: To keep the machine's old settings instead of overwriting them when the symlink replaces the file.

title: The AI review gate
purpose: See that every change an agent proposes passes a review gate before it reaches the repository.
explanation: The agent proposes edits, but nothing is merged until you approve it and the tests pass. A failing test sends the change back to the agent instead of forward to merge.
alt: A flow from your prompt to the coding agent to proposed edits, through a review gate to running the tests; a passing test goes to merge, a failing test loops back to the agent.

learning_check.question: Which test result sends a change back to the agent?
learning_check.answer: A failing test, so an unverified change never reaches merge.

title: A production team's reproducible setup
purpose: See how a team turns shared configuration into identical developer machines.
explanation: One dotfiles repo holds the shell, git, and editor config. An install script links those files onto each new laptop, and a `.nvmrc` that pins an LTS version keeps every machine on the same Node runtime.
alt: A dotfiles repo feeds an install script, which reproduces a developer laptop. A Long-Term Support policy sets the version a `.nvmrc` file pins, and that file pins the same Node version on every laptop.

learning_check.question: A new hire's Node differs from the team's. Which file makes it match?
learning_check.answer: The shared `.nvmrc`, which pins the LTS version the policy chose.

title: git bisect narrows to the bug commit
purpose: See how git bisect halves the commit range using one test until only the bug commit remains.
explanation: bisect.sh marks HEAD bad and the first commit good, then git bisect run invokes check.js at each midpoint. check.js exits 0 for good and 1 for bad, so git halves the range each step and stops at commit 5.
alt: A flow from setup-demo-repo.sh to bisect.sh, which marks the range, then loops through git bisect run and check.js exit codes until HEAD ends on commit 5.

learning_check.question: What does check.js exit 1 tell git bisect?
learning_check.answer: That the current commit is bad, so git searches the older half of the remaining range.

title: Layers of the Dev environment configurator
purpose: See the four layers of the app and that every dependency points inward, toward the domain.
explanation: React components and a hook sit in the interface layer, the generator in application, DeveloperConfig, NodeVersion and the ports in domain, and the storage, downloader, config and logger in infrastructure. Arrows point inward, so the domain knows nobody.
alt: Four layers: interface holds ConfiguratorForm and useConfigurator, application holds DotfilesGenerator, domain holds DeveloperConfig, NodeVersion and the ports, infrastructure holds LocalStorageConfigStorage, BrowserBundleDownloader, EnvConfig and ConsoleLogger; every arrow points inward.

learning_check.question: Which layer holds DeveloperConfig, and which direction do the dependencies point?
learning_check.answer: The domain, and inward — the domain depends on nothing outside itself.

title: Generate dotfiles request flow
purpose: Follow one submit through validation, generation, save, and download, including the failure path.
explanation: The form calls generate, which validates the draft into a DeveloperConfig. Invalid input throws with a code and shows a field error; valid input generates a bundle, saves the config, and downloads the installer.
alt: A sequence from Developer through ConfiguratorForm, useConfigurator, DeveloperConfig, DotfilesGenerator, ConfigStorage and BundleDownloader, branching where invalid input returns a coded error and valid input saves and downloads.

learning_check.question: Where does invalid input stop the flow?
learning_check.answer: In DeveloperConfig.create, which throws an InvalidConfigError with a code before anything is generated or saved.

title: Deployment of the static build
purpose: See the two Dockerfile stages: build the static bundle with Node, serve it with nginx.
explanation: The Dockerfile builds the app in a node stage with Vite, then copies the dist folder into an nginx stage that serves it on port 80. Configuration is baked in at build time.
alt: Two Dockerfile stages: a node:22-alpine stage runs npm run build to produce dist, and an nginx:1.27-alpine stage serves that dist folder to the browser on port 80.

learning_check.question: Which Dockerfile stage runs npm run build?
learning_check.answer: The node:22-alpine build stage; the nginx stage only serves the result.
